description: ONE PLANNED RECOGNITION EVENT: how much revenue, on what date or against which milestone, and — once it has happened — the draft journal entry that recorded it. Time-based rows carry a date and no obligation; milestone-based rows carry an obligation and become recognisable the day it is satisfied. Both shapes live in one table because they are the same row with a different trigger, and splitting them would mean every report that asks 'what is left to recognise on this contract' had to union two tables.

fields.description: What makes this row ripe. `Milestone` waits for its obligation to be satisfied — point-in-time recognition. `Time` comes due on its own date — over-time recognition, which is what a storage or management agreement earns.
fields.label: Basis

fields.description: For a milestone row: which performance obligation on this contract, matched by its text. Blank on a time row.
fields.label: Obligation

fields.description: For a time row: the date this tranche is earned. For a milestone row it is the EXPECTED date and nothing turns on it — the obligation's own `satisfied_on` is what actually decides.
fields.label: Due

fields.description: Set by recognize_revenue_milestone. Never typed: a row marked recognised by hand would claim a journal entry exists that does not.
fields.label: Recognized

fields.description: The DRAFT entry this recognition produced. Draft, like every journal entry this app writes — recognising revenue is a posting somebody signs off, not a side effect of ticking a box.
fields.label: Journal Entry

name: Revenue Recognition Schedule
